B.1 Restatement of Theorem A (Execution Stability Horizon)
[id=A2.SS1.p1.1] Consider an autoregressive reasoning trajectory as a Markov process
[id=A2.Ex10]
Zt+1∼K(⋅∣Zt),Z_{t+1}\sim K(\cdot\mid Z_{t}),
[id=A2.SS1.p1.2] where ZtZ_{t} is the latent execution state at step tt and KK is the induced transition kernel of decoding and internal updates.
Let G∈{0,1}G\in\{0,1\} denote the target conclusion (correct vs. incorrect). We define the decision advantage at step tt as the Bayes-optimal testing advantage:
[id=A2.Ex11]
ρt:=1−2Pe(t),Pe(t):=infϕPr[ϕ(Zt)≠G],\rho_{t}:=1-2P_{e}(t),\quad P_{e}(t):=\inf_{\phi}\Pr[\phi(Z_{t})\neq G],
[id=A2.SS1.p1.3] where the infimum is over all measurable predictors ϕ\phi. Hence ρt∈[0,1]\rho_{t}\in[0,1] and ρt=0\rho_{t}=0 corresponds to chance-level inference.
[id=A2.SS1.p2.1] Theorem A (informal).
If the induced kernel loses a fixed fraction of goal-relevant information per step (formalized below), then ρt\rho_{t} decays exponentially with tt, implying a finite stability horizon L∗L^{*} beyond which reliable single-path execution becomes unstable.
[id=A2.SS2]
B.2 Objects and Notation
[id=A2.SS2.p1.1] Let
[id=A2.Ex12]
Pt:=ℒ⁡(Zt∣G=1),Qt:=ℒ⁡(Zt∣G=0),P_{t}:=\mathcal{L}(Z_{t}\mid G=1),\qquad Q_{t}:=\mathcal{L}(Z_{t}\mid G=0),
[id=A2.SS2.p1.2] denote the conditional state distributions. We use total variation (TV) distance
[id=A2.Ex13]
Δt:=TV⁡(Pt,Qt)\Delta_{t}:=\mathrm{TV}(P_{t},Q_{t})
[id=A2.SS2.p1.3] as a distinguishability measure, and mutual information I⁡(G,Zt)I(G;Z_{t}) as a goal-relevant information measure.
[id=A2.SS2.p2.1] We assume balanced priors Pr⁡(G=1)=Pr⁡(G=0)=1/2\Pr(G=1)=\Pr(G=0)=1/2 for simplicity; this can be relaxed with minor constant changes.
[id=A2.SS3]
B.3 Main Assumption: Per-step Contraction of the Induced Decoding Channel
[id=A2.SS3.p1.1] The proof of Theorem A relies on a single structural property of the induced kernel.
Assumption 1 (Kernel contraction (TV form)).
[id=Thmassumption1.p1.1] There exists η∈(0,1)\eta\in(0,1) such that for any pair of input distributions μ,ν\mu,\nu over ZtZ_{t},
[id=A2.Ex14]
TV⁡(μ​K,ν​K)≤η​TV​(μ,ν),\mathrm{TV}(\mu K,\nu K)\ \leq\ \eta\,\mathrm{TV}(\mu,\nu),
[id=Thmassumption1.p1.2] where μ​K\mu K denotes the pushforward distribution after one step of the Markov kernel KK.
[id=A2.SS3.p2.1] Interpretation.
Assumption 1 isolates intrinsic process-level instability as a property of the induced decoding channel itself, independent of branching, search complexity, or task semantics. It says that one step of autoregressive execution makes two hypotheses about the goal strictly less distinguishable.
[id=A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1]
Testability.
[id=A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1] The constant η\eta is an effective contraction coefficient that can be estimated empirically by fitting distinguishability decay across controlled tasks (see Section B.6).
[id=A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2]
Sufficient conditions (informal).
[id=A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1] Assumption 1 holds for many ergodic/noisy Markov kernels with a Doeblin/minorization condition or a Dobrushin contraction coefficient strictly less than 11. This includes kernels that (i) apply a deterministic map followed by (ii) an irreducible noise channel that is independent of GG and has a uniform mixing component. Standard references on contraction coefficients and strong data processing inequalities apply (e.g., lecture notes and surveys such as [15]).
[id=A2.SS4]
B.4 From Contraction to Exponential Decay
Lemma 4 (Iterated contraction implies exponential decay in TV).
[id=Thmlemma4.p1.1] Under Assumption 1, we have
[id=A2.Ex15]
Δt≤ηt​Δ0.\Delta_{t}\leq\eta^{t}\Delta_{0}.
Proof.
[id=A2.SS4.p1.1] By definition, Pt+1=Pt​KP_{t+1}=P_{t}K and Qt+1=Qt​KQ_{t+1}=Q_{t}K. Applying Assumption 1 with μ=Pt\mu=P_{t} and ν=Qt\nu=Q_{t} yields
[id=A2.Ex16]
Δt+1=TV⁡(Pt​K,Qt​K)≤η​TV​(Pt,Qt)=η​Δt.\Delta_{t+1}=\mathrm{TV}(P_{t}K,Q_{t}K)\leq\eta\,\mathrm{TV}(P_{t},Q_{t})=\eta\,\Delta_{t}.
[id=A2.SS4.p1.2] Iterating gives Δt≤ηt​Δ0\Delta_{t}\leq\eta^{t}\Delta_{0}.
∎
Lemma 5 (Decision advantage is controlled by distinguishability).
[id=Thmlemma5.p1.1] With balanced priors, the Bayes-optimal testing advantage satisfies
[id=A2.Ex17]
ρt≤Δt.\rho_{t}\leq\Delta_{t}.
Proof.
[id=A2.SS4.p2.1] For testing G∈{0,1}G\in\{0,1\} from ZtZ_{t} under equal priors, the Bayes error satisfies
[id=A2.Ex18]
Pe​(t)=12​(1−TV⁡(Pt,Qt)),P_{e}(t)=\tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(1-\mathrm{TV}(P_{t},Q_{t})\bigr),
[id=A2.SS4.p2.2] and hence ρt=1−2​Pe​(t)=TV⁡(Pt,Qt)=Δt\rho_{t}=1-2P_{e}(t)=\mathrm{TV}(P_{t},Q_{t})=\Delta_{t}.
(If one uses an alternative definition of ρt\rho_{t} (e.g., via a fixed decision rule), the inequality form ρt≤Δt\rho_{t}\leq\Delta_{t} still holds.)
∎
Proof sketch of Theorem A.
[id=A2.SS4.p3.1] Combine Lemma 4 and Lemma 5:
[id=A2.Ex19]
ρt≤Δt≤ηt​Δ0.\rho_{t}\leq\Delta_{t}\leq\eta^{t}\Delta_{0}.
[id=A2.SS4.p3.2] Let ρ0:=Δ0\rho_{0}:=\Delta_{0} and γ:=−ln⁡η>0\gamma:=-\ln\eta>0. Then
[id=A2.Ex20]
ρt≤ρ0​e−γ​t.\rho_{t}\leq\rho_{0}e^{-\gamma t}.
[id=A2.SS4.p3.3] Solving ρt≤τ\rho_{t}\leq\tau yields the critical horizon
[id=A2.Ex21]
L∗=1γ​ln⁡ρ0τ.L^{*}=\frac{1}{\gamma}\ln\frac{\rho_{0}}{\tau}.
[id=A2.SS4.p3.4] ∎

B.5 Equivalent Formulation via SDPI (Mutual Information Form)
[id=A2.SS5.p1.1] Some readers may prefer an information-theoretic statement that cleanly separates (i) per-step information loss from (ii) hypothesis-testing conversion.
Assumption 2 (Per-step SDPI (MI form)).
[id=Thmassumption2.p1.1] There exists α∈(0,1)\alpha\in(0,1) such that
[id=A2.E19]

[id=A2.SS5.p2.1] Assumption 2 is a strong data processing inequality (SDPI) for the induced channel Zt↦Zt+1Z_{t}\mapsto Z_{t+1}, commonly satisfied by mixing/noisy channels under suitable regularity [15].
Lemma 6 (SDPI implies exponential decay of MI).
[id=Thmlemma6.p1.1] Under Assumption 2, I⁡(G,Zt)≤αt​I​(G,Z0)I(G;Z_{t})\leq\alpha^{t}I(G;Z_{0}).
Proof.

[id=Thmlemma7.p1.1] There exists a universal constant c>0c>0 such that
[id=A2.Ex22]
ρt≤c​I⁡(G,Zt).\rho_{t}\leq c\sqrt{I(G;Z_{t})}.
Proof sketch.

B.6 Operational Definition: Estimating α⁡(C)\alpha(C) or η⁡(C)\eta(C) from Controlled Tasks
[id=A2.SS6.p1.1] To make the contraction assumption reviewer-auditable, we propose an operational estimate.
[id=A2.SS6.p2.1] Fix a controlled task family indexed by a complexity parameter CC (e.g., synthetic legal reasoning instances with controlled distractor load, depth, or aliasing). For each tt, measure the Bayes error (or a calibrated proxy) of predicting GG from ZtZ_{t}, yielding Pe​(t,C)P_{e}(t;C) and advantage
[id=A2.Ex24]
ρt​(C)=1−2​Pe​(t,C).\rho_{t}(C)=1-2P_{e}(t;C).
[id=A2.SS6.p2.2] Fit an exponential curve over the range where decay is approximately geometric:
[id=A2.Ex25]
ρt​(C)≈ρ0​(C)​e−γ⁡(C)​t.\rho_{t}(C)\approx\rho_{0}(C)\,e^{-\gamma(C)t}.
[id=A2.SS6.p2.3] Then define the effective coefficients
[id=A2.Ex26]
η⁡(C):=e−γ⁡(C),α⁡(C):=e−2​γ​(C).\eta(C):=e^{-\gamma(C)},\qquad\alpha(C):=e^{-2\gamma(C)}.
[id=A2.SS6.p2.4] This turns the abstract stability assumption into an empirically estimable quantity.
[id=A2.SS7]
B.7 Toy Numerical Illustration (Not a Claim about LLMs)
[id=A2.SS7.p1.1] To illustrate the mechanism in a minimal setting, consider the 1D autoregressive chain
[id=A2.Ex27]
Zt+1=a​Zt+ϵt,ϵt∼𝒩⁡(0,σ2),Z_{t+1}=aZ_{t}+\epsilon_{t},\qquad\epsilon_{t}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^{2}),
[id=A2.SS7.p1.2] with |a|<1|a|<1. Two initial hypotheses about Z0Z_{0} become less distinguishable over time, producing geometric decay in any reasonable distinguishability proxy.
import numpy as np
np.random.seed(42)
T = 100
eta_est = 0.95
delta = [0.5]
for t in range(1, T):
delta.append(eta_est * delta[-1])
# delta[t] decays geometrically; gamma = -ln(eta_est)
[id=A2.SS7.p3.1] This toy example is included solely to visualize geometric decay; it is not intended as a faithful mechanistic model of Transformer internals.
[id=A2.SS8]
B.8 Remarks on Scope
Remark 1 (What this appendix does and does not claim).
[id=Thmremark1.p1.1] Theorem A is a structural result: once the induced decoding dynamics admit a strict per-step contraction (TV) or SDPI (MI), exponential decay of decision advantage follows. Deriving an exact contraction constant from specific architectural primitives (e.g., attention softmax) is a separate, more model-specific question and is left for future work.
